differences.what: Actual master reviewed: pointed north cone and lower connector retain the integrated flat north facade and curved west drum. The corrected north service door/window and stable roof junction remain visible.

T-2228 cupola body: the dovecote body now stands clear of the stable ridge with both pigeon-hole tiers in open air, and the pyramid rises well above the north gable apex as the photograph shows (body top 41.0, apex 47.0 ft ng, from 38.9/43.3). Read against the gable apex and ridge crest: apex about 35 px over the gable apex against the photograph's 45 (within the +/-1 ft bound), pyramid slope apex-to-SW-eave 60,73 px against 58,82.

T-2849, reviewed from the rebaked master: the cupola body is now granite as the print shows its coursed shaft below the band (it was boarding), on stone landing ledges 0.25 ft deep; the gable's ledge now carries the two corbels this print shows under it, with the 5-3-1 pigeon holes at the spacing HABS photograph 15 measures. Still open after T-3030: the cupola's corners carry a dark vertical strip from the band to the roof that neither northwest print shows (T-3036); the stable end sits about 28 px off because this camera is fitted at the Prairie corner (T-2758).

T-3025, ruled: the covering this print reads slate-grey, the cupola's pyramid included, is the 1963 tar HABS records over the tiles (data p. 21), not the 1904 surface. The roofs were red baked, unglazed terracotta tile (Glessner 1923, HABS data p. 13; HABS's 1963 survey finds terracotta under the tar, which excludes slate), and the record lays that. Colour in a monochrome print is not shown; nothing is rebaked. docs/RESEARCH/glessner-roof-covering-T-3025/README.md.

T-2228: the cupola centre reads about 22 px (roughly 4 ft by parallax) north of the owner-directed S14.6, kept; the whole stable roof reads about 28 px low in this camera, which is camera/height uncertainty, not yet a roof correction. T-2758: it is the camera, not the roof. This camera's only vertical controls are the grade and eave at the Prairie corner (W 0), 141 ft east of the stable, so at the stable it draws 14.6 px a foot where the carriage doorway (sheet 2 jambs W 134.9-147.0, sheet 5 soffit 12.6 ft) measures 13.85 in the print. Re-solved with the doorway's four corners added (eye height or image lean free in turn), it reads the gable's coping apex at 38.1-38.6 ft and the cupola's apex at 45.5-46.3 ft on the model's centre (model 39.6 and 47.0), and the doorway as a bare ruler reads the coping apex at 38.8 ft. The residual of about 1 ft is inside the ridge's 1.5 ft tolerance and is no larger than the Cornell view's re-solved disagreement with it (38.3-39.5 ft), so the roof is not changed. The 4 ft parallax was not a reading: every control in this photograph lies in the north face, so its depth is free: with the pixel aspect let go, which those controls cannot measure, fits of one RMS (3.9 px) slide the cupola from S14.4 at square pixels to S10.4 at an aspect of 1.06 while the gable's height does not move. The Cornell view, re-solved on two faces, puts it at S13.0-13.2, about 1.5 ft north of S14.6, which does not hold up as a question for the owner. The doorway re-solve is not adopted here: it moves the north tower's finial about 9 px off the print where this camera holds it to 1.5 px, so one level pinhole does not fit both ends of this print. data/comparisons/glessner/stable-roof-heights.json (tools/glessner_stable_roof_read.py).

The later overhead garage door, closed loft opening, vehicles, utilities and surrounding1963 street fabric are not carried back as1904 details. This crop alone does not establish exact original color.

T-2848 light: the render now takes the photograph's own sun, low from the east-north-east (camera solve.light), so the 18th Street wall is raked from the left and the stable's west end falls in shade as in the print; it no longer uses the review default. The elevation is a plausible summer-morning height, not a measured shadow length.
T-2848: the stone in this print is darkened by decades of city soot, so its tone in the 1960s photograph is not its 1887 tone; the render's clean stone is not compared against it.

T-2873, re-rendered on the widened north stack (7.1 ft, read through HABS 14's camera): the stack's silhouette through the date stones reads 61 px (x 231-292) against the photograph's 58.5 (x 234.5-293), where the 5.1-ft stack drew about 51; the lit face's corner with the west side falls within about 2 px of the photograph's. The 3.5 px at the east edge is within this level camera's reading of the roof (about 2 ft low at the stable).

T-3030, reviewed from the rebaked master: the long dark band running east from under the gable's arch, past the gable's own edge, is the hoist stone's cast shadow under this print's raking sun, not a beam; the stone itself, its nose where a 3-4 ft projection puts it, is now built 4.0 ft out as a tapered cantilever. The render's review light does not cast that shadow, which is lighting, not geometry. The cupola's landing ledges now wrap its corners as the print shows.

T-3031, reviewed from the rebaked master: the cupola is read from both northwest prints at once through the cameras T-2758 re-solved on measured controls at the stable, each with its local offset taken out at the north gable's coping apex (tools/glessner_cupola_read.py, data/comparisons/glessner/stable-cupola.json). The two prints agree on the eave (41.9 and 41.75 ft) and jointly fit a 5.5 ft body (half 2.73 +/-0.18), a 0.72 ft eave, the eave at 41.87 and the apex at 48.19 ft, centre S14.76 (5.3 px RMS over 12 picks, against 11.5 and 13.8 px for the build as it stood). Built: body 5.5 ft square with its top at 42.0 ft (was 6.0 ft, 41.0), apex 48.2 (was 47.0), eave 0.75 ft out (was 1.25), the pigeon-hole band raised with it to 39.5-41.6 ft; centre S14.6 kept. The 27-32 px by which this print had seemed to stand the cupola higher than HABS photograph 1 was mostly the committed camera's: through it the render is not a measure of the cupola's height at the stable end (T-2758). Through this committed camera, which is fitted at the Prairie corner, the rebuilt apex now stands about 61 px over the gable apex against the print's 52 (the earlier build stood about 44): the camera's own depth at the stable (it reads the cupola's centre at S11.0) is the residual, not the cupola.

T-3036, reviewed from the rebaked master: the dark vertical strip that ran down each corner of the cupola's body, from under the eave through the pigeon-hole band to the roof, is gone; the corners read as one turned stone face, as the print shows them. It was the body's four walls each running the full plan width, so each wall's 0.08 m end lay in its neighbour's face, half of them wound inward: the east and west walls now take the corners, the north and south walls butt inside them, and every edge face of the walls and landing ledges is turned outward. No dimension of the cupola moved.

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown}. A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
